title: Confederation of the Rhine
capsule: The Confederation of the Rhine (Rheinbund) was a coalition of sixteen initially, and ultimately thirty-nine, German states established by Napoleon on 12 July 1806 following his victory at Austerlitz. Its formation triggered the abdication of Holy Roman Emperor Francis II on 6 August 1806, dissolving an institution that had existed in various forms since 962. Member princes provided Napoleon with military contingents — ultimately some 119,000 troops — and the Confederation served as an eastern buffer zone shielding France from Prussian and Austrian counterattack. After Napoleon's catastrophic defeat in Russia and the Battle of Leipzig (16–19 October 1813), the member states defected; the Confederation was formally dissolved and replaced by the German Confederation at the Congress of Vienna in 1815.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution.
